subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Bloc Sauvage
spec.description: A raw-concrete brutalist housing block: a deep pilotis plinth, a repetitive slab tower of recessed window boxes and cantilevered balcony bands, a taller stair core of vertical fins at the back, and a cluttered mechanical roofscape.
spec.layout: The model is a vertical composition, +Z facing the street. From the ground up: a massive cast plinth (0 to 1.6 m) with a front colonnade of chunky square pilotis, a recessed rust-red entrance with a heavy cantilevered concrete canopy at the front, and a low ramp slab running down its left side; the plinth is the only part whose lowest points touch y = 0. Above the plinth rises the main tower slab (x -2.8..2.8, z -2.6..3.4, 8 storeys of 1.3 m up to y 12.0): a strict grid of deep-set window boxes in dark glass under proud concrete lintels, horizontal balcony bands cantilevering off the front bay, ribbed precast panels and a vertical stair-slot of lit amber windows near its left edge. At the back (-Z) sits the service core (x -2.9..-0.9, z -4.2..-2.6), a taller bookend slab of closely spaced vertical concrete fins with narrow slit windows that rises past the tower to y 13.4 and is capped by its own thick crown slab. On the tower roof (from y 11.9) a mechanical penthouse, rusted vents, a squat cylindrical water tank, a parapet with drainage scuppers and a thin whip antenna carry the block to its 14.2 m top. The style shows everywhere: chunky chamfered concrete masses, board-formed texture suggested by subtle concrete-tone variation between panels, deep shadow gaps between every projecting element, utilitarian metalwork in rust and steel, and strict repetition as ornament.

parts.builds: The ground-level base of the block, floor: true. A heavy cast ground slab from y 0 to 1.2 spanning the full footprint (with a stepped-up podium deck to y 1.6 under the tower footprint), built as chunky concrete masses in concrete/concreteShade tones with sharp chamfered edges. Along the front (+Z) a colonnade of 6 square pilotis (about 0.55 m square, concreteLight) standing on plinths, supporting a deep cast lintel band at y 1.6. Between the columns the recessed entrance: a dark shadow-box void in concreteDeep holding double rust-red doors (doorRust) with a mustard push-bar, a signCream enamel plaque with a block-letter building number ('B-7' as small extruded parts or a decal), and a round bulkhead lamp. A thick cantilevered concrete canopy (concrete) juts ~1.2 m past the front face at y 2.1 above the doors with two downpipes (railingSteel). On the left side a ramp slab rises from y 0 to the podium deck with a low kerb and a simple steel handrail (railingSteel) on thin posts. Back and sides of the plinth are blind concrete wall with horizontal board-form joint lines as thin recessed strips (concreteShade), a rust service door with a mustard frame at the back right, and small square grilles (railingSteel) near the base. Scatter two or three squat concrete bollards at the front edge. Budget the detail on the front; the back stays austere.
parts.attaches: Its top deck (mount plinthTop at y 1.6) carries the tower body and the service core; the core also lands on the back strip of the plinth. The canopy overlaps the tower's lowest front band by design — keep it below the tower's first window sill.

parts.builds: The main housing slab, the hero of the model, from y 1.6 to 12.0 (8 storeys of 1.3 m each). Build the slab as a boxy concrete mass (concrete) and carve the rhythm with parts, not smoothness: on every storey a repeating grid of deep-set window boxes — recessed dark glass panes (glass, a few glassDark, and 2-3 amberLit windows glowing near the stair slot) pushed ~0.25 m back in their reveals, each reveal built from concreteShade jamb, head and sill parts with a proud concreteLight lintel band above running the full facade width. Front facade: a wide central bay of paired windows flanked by blind concrete piers, plus two cantilevered balcony bands (concreteLight deck slabs ~0.35 m thick projecting ~0.6 m) at storeys 3 and 6 running across most of the front, each with a railing of thin vertical steel bars (railingSteel) and a rust-red privacy screen panel (doorRust) on one balcony. Left edge: a vertical stair slot — a full-height recessed strip (concreteDeep) with narrow slit windows, one lit amber per landing. Right facade: mostly blind with ribbed precast panels (alternating concrete/concreteShade vertical fins via extrude) and one column of small square windows. Back facade is simple: the repeating window grid continues but plain, with no balconies. Add two thin drainage pipes (railingSteel) running down a front pier, small mustard-painted balcony door frames, and a tiny signCream floor-number plaque beside the stair slot on storey 1.
parts.attaches: Sits on the plinth deck at mount plinthTop (y 1.6); its back face at z -2.6 is the shared seam with the service core (mount coreSeam, which spans x -2.9..-0.9 on that face); its roof at y 12.0 is mount towerRoof where the roof plant sits. Balconies may pass slightly over the plinth's front edge.

parts.builds: The stair/service core bookending the tower at the back, rising from y 1.6 to a thick crown slab at y 13.0-13.4 — about 1.4 m taller than the tower so its silhouette breaks the roofline. The core is a slab (concreteShade) of closely spaced vertical concrete fins: about 10 extruded fins (alternating concreteLight/concrete) standing ~0.15 m proud, running the full height, wrapping the front face that looks over the tower roof. Between fins, deep shadow slots (concreteDeep) with sparse narrow slit windows: a vertical strip of glass (glassDark) slits every other storey, two of them amberLit (the stairwell glowing). At the seam with the tower (mount coreSeam at z -2.6) a buttress-like thickened pier joins the two masses. On the back face, blind concrete with two rows of tiny square vents (railingSteel) and one rust-painted service door at podium level. The crown: a heavy cap slab (concrete) overhanging the fins by ~0.2 m on all sides, with a low parapet kerb (concreteShade), a small mechanical housing box (concreteLight) on top, a steel ladder (railingSteel) from the tower roof up the core's front face, and a tiny signCream plate. This part is the model's second-tallest landmark — keep it austere, vertical and rhythmic.
parts.attaches: Lands on the back strip of the plinth at y 1.6 and welds to the tower body along the shared face at z -2.6 (mount coreSeam, x -2.9..-0.9, y 1.6..12.0); it stands clear of the tower roof, rising beside mount towerRoof's area.

parts.builds: The mechanical roofscape above the tower, from y 11.9 (overlapping the tower's top 0.1 m so it seats) up to y 14.2. First a parapet: a low concrete kerb (concreteLight) around the tower roof edge with rusted scupper drains (ventRust) poking through at intervals and dark rain stains (thin concreteShade strips) below two of them. Inside, a mechanical penthouse box (concrete) with a corrugated rhythm of vertical panel ribs (roofMetal), a rusted steel door (doorRust) with a mustard frame, a small grille, and a stubby steel flue (railingSteel) rising from its roof with a rain cap. Beside it, a squat cylindrical water tank (concreteShade) on 4 short chunky legs, banded with two rust hoops (ventRust) and topped with a conical lid and a tiny access hatch. A cluster of 3-4 mushroom vent stacks (concreteLight with roofMetal cowls) near the parapet, connected by a low pipe run (railingSteel) along the deck. A lattice-TV antenna or whip mast (railingSteel) on a small concrete base carries the model to its full 14.2 m: a thin vertical mast with two short cross-arms and a small red aircraft warning lamp disc at the tip (amberLit, glowing). A couple of small rooftop details — a ventilation grille frame, a painted number '08' in signCream on the penthouse wall — finish it. Keep the mass low and clustered toward the back-left so the tower's front roof edge stays clean.
parts.attaches: Sits on the tower roof at mount towerRoof (y 12.0, over the tower's x -2.8..2.8 / z -2.6..3.4 footprint, box bottom 11.9 to seat into the roof deck); it stands beside the service core's crown, which rises independently to y 13.4 — keep clear of core's x -2.9..-0.9 / z -4.2..-2.6 column.
